item.title: Thieves apprehended after several 911 calls
item.description: Fayette County Sheriff Keith Korenek reported that on Friday, Feb. 27 at approximately 6:05 a.m., deputies Terry Guentert, James Ulbig, and Ty Roggenkamp received a series of 911 calls stating that one or two subjects had been beating on windows and doors and going through vehicles.

item.title: Geesaman unseats Kitzman in Primary
item.description: In the Republican Primary held on March 3, challenger Dennis Geesaman defeated incumbent Stan Kitzman in the race for the Texas House of Representatives District 85 seat. The former Flatonia mayor and city councilman won by a 3,922vote margin, getting 1,006 more votes than Kitzman in Fayette County.

item.title: $14 million financing package approved to pay for City projects
item.description: After receiving details on the scope of work and financing options for renovating two buildings at a workshop, the Schulenburg City Council approved moving forward with securing $14 million in certificates of obligation at its meeting on Tuesday, March 3.

item.title: Plans for parks & rec presented to Council
item.description: Alarge-format booklet mapping out potential upgrades to Schulenburg’s two public parks was presented to the City Council at its meeting on Tuesday, March 3. The master plan included input from the community since the project was initiated last July with the City’s hiring of the firm Burditt.

item.title: Financing increased for City projects
item.description: Two weeks after approving $14 million in financing through certificates of obligations for building renovations and other projects, the Schulenburg City Council increased the total to $15 million at its regular meeting Monday, March 16.

item.title: Burn ban reinstated Monday
item.description: Just three days after not extending the burn ban in effect since Sept. 11, the Fayette County Commissioners Court put one back in place at an emergency meeting on Monday.

item.title: Election issues reviewed
item.description: With three of the five members present, the Fayette County Commissioners Court met on Thursday, March 12. On hand were Precinct 1 Commissioners Jason McBroom, Precinct 2 Commissioner Clint Sternadel, and Precinct 4 Commissioner Drew Brossmann.

item.title: Next year’s school calendar includes later start, five fewer days
item.description: After hearing Superintendent Lee Hafley’s modifications to two other proposed calendars for the 2026-27 school year, the Schulenburg ISD Board of Trustees voted unanimously to go with his option at its meeting Monday, March 23.

item.title: School board trustees approve early resignation notice incentive by 5-2 vote
item.description: Revisiting a topic that was discussed and tabled at last month’s meeting, the Schulenburg ISD Board of Trustees voted on March 23 in favor of incentivising employees under contract who plan to leave to submit their resignations early.

item.title: This year’s Sausagefest scheduled for April 11
item.description: The 11th Annual Schulenburg Sausagefest will be held downtown on Saturday, April 11. The event will take place on North Main Street between LyonsAvenue and WoltersAvenue, including the Railroad Park.
